ImageDescription.value:
Mallishwara Mudi – The Sacred Peak of Attappady

Mallishwara Mudi (മല്ലിശ്വര മുടി) is a prominent mountain peak located in the Attappady region of Palakkad district, Kerala, India. Rising majestically in the backdrop of the Silent Valley biosphere, this peak holds deep spiritual and cultural significance for the local tribal communities, especially the Irula and Muduga tribes.

The name Mallishwara is believed to be derived from "Mallikarjuna," a form of Lord Shiva. The mountain is revered as a sacred abode of Lord Shiva, and when viewed from certain angles—especially during early morning or dusk—the silhouette of the peak strikingly resembles the matted hair (jata) of Lord Shiva, evoking imagery of his iconic conical hair-knot.

Geographical Significance: Location: Attappady, Palakkad, Kerala

Range: Nilgiri Hills, part of the Western Ghats

Closest Wildlife Area: Silent Valley National Park

Elevation: Approx. 1,600–1,800 meters (unofficial estimate)

Cultural Importance: Worshipped by indigenous tribal communities

Considered the ‘Thirumudi’ (sacred crown) of Lord Shiva

Pilgrimages and traditional offerings are made to the mountain from the foothills

Tribal legends narrate the presence of divine energy in the mountain’s core

In the Photograph:

The provided image captures the front view of Mallishwara Mudi under natural sunlight. The sharp central peak symbolizes the divine form of Shiva’s hair-lock (jata), and the surrounding landscape enhances its serene and mystical presence. The green meadow in the foreground opens up to the dramatic silhouette of the hills, making it a spiritual and natural marvel of Kerala.

Categories.value: Human genetics|Population genetics|Genetic structure|Human genetic structures

ImageDescription.value:
qpGraph model of N and S ancestries of South Asians:
The qpGraph reported here places the obtained N and S deconvoluted ancestries (represented here by Gujaratis_N and Irula_S, respectively) within the broader scenario of within Eurasia splits and subsequent admixtures. Alternative trees involving a different Onge/Han/S split order, or a reverse Steppe_EMBA – S admixture direction yielded f4 outliers and an overall poorer fit. Final score: 3,061.001, degrees of freedom: 2, no f2 outliers, no f4 outliers, worst f-stat: 1.747.

ImageDescription.value:
An ancestry map of the genetic makeup of South Asian populations, showing the average amount of West-Eurasian and East-Eurasian ancestry components.

As the AASI component is a simulation, the percentage may vary slightly between different models.

The used data set is freely available (G25). The models were run and tested with Vahaduo. The AASI model is based on a simulation: AASI_DMXX. This simulation was based on Irula, Paniya and Mala samples.

The model was tested and errornous results were minimized. The results overall correspond with Changmai et al. 2022 (Figure 3:https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-26799-3)
